trust_decision.summary: URI.parse decides which part of an input string is the hostname. The regex that normalises slashes and backslashes after web schemes only matches lower-case schemes, so a mixed-case scheme (hTTps:////host) skips it and the parsed hostname differs from what browsers resolve.

landing_point.why: This is the only regex in URI.parse that names the http/https/ftp/ws schemes and handles excess slashes. The advisory (hostname confusion from excess slashes) leads straight to it.

fix_sites.entry_point: URI(string) / new URI(string) / uri.href(string) -> URI.parse (src/URI.js:1256); also public URI.parse(string)
same public API, minified distribution build of src/URI.js
fix_sites.module_kind: generated minified copy (build artefact, not an independent implementation)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/URI.min.js is only the generated minified copy of the same function (fix.diff:26-27); there is no independent second route.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Nothing of substance. Every string route (constructor, href, resource, origin setter) funnels into the single regex at src/URI.js:516. Only the minified build copy could be dismissed, as 'generated, rebuilt later'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The output must keep the scheme's case (protocol stays 'hTTps', _url 'hTTps://attacker.com/'). Non-web schemes and URNs such as 'mailto:' or 'urn:' must not be rewritten to 'scheme://'. Lowercasing the input or widening the scheme list would break these.

O6_input_shapes: mixed- or upper-case web scheme followed by excess forward slashes (hTTps://////host)
mixed-case scheme with backslashes or no slashes (HTTP:\\host, HTTP:host), via the same [/\\]* class at src/URI.js:516

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ensureValidHostname compares the protocol against hostProtocols case-sensitively, so an upper-case scheme escapes the empty-hostname rejection
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same kind of case-sensitive scheme comparison already exists here. A maintainer adding a scheme allow-list check elsewhere would naturally write it the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: leading whitespace or a control character before the scheme also stops the anchored ^ regex from matching
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Nothing trims the input before line 516. Upstream reportedly fixed these later as separate advisories, so they are realistic, but they are input-shape variants at the same single line.

O9_family: URL parsing / hostname confusion (parser differential leading to open redirect or SSRF allow-list bypass); the advisory's CWE-639 label does not fit

O10_build.toolchain: plain JS; src/URI.js needs no npm scripts or dependencies. Tests are QUnit (browser harness test/index.html) and can run in node with a small shim
O10_build.project_tests: test/urls.js (URL table incl. 'excessive slash protocol https' at test/urls.js:2282), driven by test/test.js

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the /i flag to the regex at src/URI.js:516 (this is exactly the published fix).

out_of_scope_notes: src/URI.js:1087: case-sensitive hostProtocols check in ensureValidHostname. This is a different protection (empty-hostname rejection); not pursued.
urijs had a run of 2022 parser advisories (backslash, whitespace, control characters); not pursued beyond the O8b note.
